To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We show that the complexity and diversity of the transcription factor repertoire in Capsaspora is strikingly high.

1. the unicellular amoeboid holozoa Capsaspora owcwczarzaki has an unexpected repertoire of metazoanspecific transcription factors (TF); 2. phylogenetic and comparative analyses with a broad sampling of eukaryotic genomes allowed us to formulate novel hypotheses on the origin and evolution in the metazoan lineage of developmental TF;
the unicellular holozoa Capsaspora owcwczarzaki has a surprisingly complex set of metazoan developmental transcription factors, which are not all present in choanoflagelletes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of metazoan TF families and the emergence of the metazoan body plan.
the evolution of transcription factors, and how they have been involved in the origin of metazoan animals.
understanding the evolution and diversification of the TF repertoire during the emergence of the metazoan lineage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TF repertoire of the holozoans is a mosaic of metazoan, eumetazoans, and non-metazoan components.
metazoan TF repertoire is not a single entity but rather a complex of different components that have evolved at different times and rates.
metazoan-specific transcriptional regulatory networks evolved gradually, and not in a step-wise fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TFs of the unicellular holozoa are not only more similar to those of choanoflagelates and metazoan animals but also more similar to each other than to the TFs of fungi, plants, or other protist groups.

the evolution of animal transcription factors is more complex than previously thought, and that a large number of metazoan-specific TF families emerged after the divergence of choanoflagelates from the animal lineage, with a possible role in the evolution of animal development and body plan complexity.
the evolution of the TF repertoire has been punctuated by several bursts of gene gain and loss, with the origin of metazoans being a major one.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the origin of the TF repertoire of animals is much more complex than previously thought and that the evolution of metazoans was accompanied by a massive diversification of their TFs, which is consistent with the emergence of new developmental pathways and the acquisition of complex morphologies.
the evolution of the metazoan TF repertoire was complex and involved a combination of lineage-specific and ancestral events.
the origin of animal development was preceded by a long evolutionary history of TF families, which was punctuated by several bursts of diversification.
